error: The research question asks which genes switch their dominant isoform between treated and control (atopic dermatitis lesional vs control skin) — this requires transcript/isoform-level quantification (e.g., per-transcript TPM/counts from Salmon, or exon/junction usage data) to compute isoform fractions and detect dominant-isoform switching (a DTU/IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR-style analysis). The persisted data profile for this analysis states the input is GENE-LEVEL counts only (counts.csv, 12000 x 13, 'Gene-level counts from salmon as delivered; the record does not say whether the length correction o…'), with no transcript-level counts/TPM file present among the two input files (counts.csv and metadata.csv). Isoform-switch detection is mathematically impossible from gene-level aggregated counts — the per-transcript proportions needed to define a 'dominant isoform' are not recoverable from a matrix that has already summed across transcripts per gene. No reference dataset, gene set, or reprocessing step available to this planner can regenerate transcript-level quantification from gene-level counts; regenerating it would require access to the original Salmon quant.sf transcript-level output or raw reads, neither of which is listed as available input. Rather than submit a plan whose central step (isoform-switch detection) is guaranteed to fail or produce fabricated results by misusing gene-level data as if it were transcript-level, I am stopping to flag this: the analysis needs transcript-level abundance (e.g., quant.sf per sample, or a transcript x sample TPM/count matrix) for the same 12 samples, not the gene-level counts.csv currently provisioned. If transcript-level quantification can be supplied or located, a DTU-style analysis (e.g., using transcript proportions and a statistical test for isoform-switching per gene, comparable to IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR/DEXSeq-style methods) can be planned against it.
